questions.q: A company stores compliance data in S3 and auditors require an audit trail of every access to the encryption keys. Which encryption option meets this?
options: Client-side encryption with no AWS service
questions.explanation: SSE-KMS with a customer-managed KMS key gives CloudTrail logging of every key use plus a key policy you control. SSE-S3 has no key-usage audit trail.

questions.q: An instance in a private subnet must download OS patches from the internet without being reachable from the internet. What do you deploy?
options: NAT Gateway in a public subnet + route from private subnet
VPC peering to a public VPC
questions.explanation: NAT Gateway gives outbound-only internet access. IGW + public IP would make it inbound-reachable.

questions.q: A mobile app lets users sign in with Google. The app needs to call AWS services on the user's behalf without storing long-lived credentials. What's the mechanism?
options: Cognito Identity Pool issuing STS credentials via AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity
Long-lived IAM access keys in the app
questions.explanation: Cognito identity pools federate the OIDC token into temporary STS credentials. IAM users or long-lived keys embedded in apps are anti-patterns.

questions.q: A public-facing web app behind CloudFront suffers repeated SQL injection attempts from known bad IP ranges. Cheapest AWS-native mitigation?
options: AWS WAF on the CloudFront distribution with managed SQLi rules and IP match rules
Move app to private subnet only
NACL deny rules on the origin subnets
questions.explanation: WAF at the edge (CloudFront) with managed rule groups blocks L7 attacks cheaply. Shield Advanced is for large-scale DDoS cost protection, not the first-line answer for injection.
